page: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.12xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, providing 48 burstable vCPUs across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. The CPU features 480 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside support for Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512 vector acceleration. The system lacks local hardware GPUs, directing all processing to the x86 compute units.

The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 7 GHz, establishing an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU core. Local storage is not bundled, necessitating external networked block volumes for operational and persistent disk access. Network interfaces provide a baseline bandwidth of 11 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with the hardware configuration.

Benchmark results show balanced compute output and strong memory-oriented metrics. The instance delivers 3839.06 GB/sec in small-block cached read bandwidth, 192.76 GB/sec in large-block uncached read throughput, and handles 87.47 million Redis set operations per second. The burstable CPU architecture provides a cost-effective design for fluctuating enterprise workloads rather than continuous 100 percent core saturation. This hardware profile aligns with large in-memory caches, relational database systems, static web infrastructure, and small-model machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.12xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by a 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6975P-C x86_64 processor with 24 physical cores and 48 burstable vCPUs, it includes 480 MB of L3 cache and support for AMX and AVX-512 extensions. The server is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations, while baseline network throughput reaches 11 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations reflect strong memory read bandwidth of up to 3839.06 GB/sec cached, alongside high-throughput Redis operations reaching 87.47 million operations per second. The burstable processor profile offers an economical trade-off for varying utilization patterns, making it suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, database operations, in-memory caching systems, and lightweight LLM inference tasks.
